questions_and_answers.question_text: What are the two uses of gǎnjué?
After which two kinds of verb can lái be used as a directional ending?
What may the thing that lái refers to be, in the sentence?
What must happen to dào and lai in sentence 7B?
Write the Chinese for "How do you feel?"
Write the Chinese for "Sit down and I'll go get you a cup of tea."

answers.answer_text: Kuài zuòxia, wǒ qù gěi ni dào bēi chá lai.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Contrast Tā pǎolai le with Tā xiělai yìfēng xìn le.

answers.answer_text: In the first, the SUBJECT (tā) comes here; in the second, the OBJECT (xìn) comes here.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Don't forget to bring your girlfriend tomorrow too."

answers.answer_text: Bié wàngle míngtian yě bǎ nǐde nǚpéngyou dàilai.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the alternative form of zuòxia?

articles.text:
7. A: Lǎo Wáng, wǒ jīntian gǎnjué    Lǎo Wáng, I feel awful today.
      hěn bù shūfu.
   B: Kuài zuòxia, wǒ qù gěi ni      Sit down and I'll go get you a cup
      dào bēi chá lai.                of tea.

Notes on No. 7

gǎnjué: "to feel; feeling." In 7A, gǎnjué is used as a VERB.

Nǐ gǎnjué zěnmeyàng?             How do you feel?
Wǒ gǎnjué tā jīntian yǒu diǎnr   I get the feeling he's a little
bù gāoxìng.                      unhappy today.

Here is an example of gǎnjué used as a NOUN:

Zhèi shi wǒde gǎnjué, nǐde       That's my feeling; what is your
kànfǎ zěnmeyàng?                 opinion?

zuòxia: "to sit down." Also zuòxialai.

dào...lai: Dào is "to pour"; dàolai is "to pour and bring here." There are two things to notice about lái as a DIRECTIONAL ENDING:

1) Lái can be used after verbs which tell of MOVEMENT from one place to another (like pǎo, "to run"), OR after verbs which describe an action WITHOUT movement from one place to another (such as dào, "to pour").

2) The thing lái refers to, which ends up "here," may be the SUBJECT or the OBJECT of the sentence. In Tā pǎolai le, "He ran here," it is the subject tā who comes here. In Tā xiělai yìfēng xìn le, "He has written a letter which has come here," it is the object xìn which comes here.

You will often SPLIT lái from the verb by inserting an object, as in sentence 7B. In fact, in 7B, dào and lai MUST be split up; lái may not precede the object.

Nǐ nǎr jièlai zhème yíliàng pò   Where did you borrow such a beat-up
chē?!                            old car from?
Wǒ zuì xǐhuan nǐ cóng Shànghǎi   I like the sweater you bought in
mǎilaide nèijiàn máoyī.          Shanghai best.
Nǐ shénme shíhou yǒu shíjiān,    When you get the time, give me a call,
dǎ ge diànhuà lai, wǒmen yìqǐ    and we'll go see a movie together.
qù kàn diànyǐng.
Bié wàngle míngtian yě bǎ nǐde   Don't forget to bring your girlfriend
nǚpéngyou dàilai.                tomorrow too.
